misconceptions.description: Auditing your workflow from memory instead of logging where time and steps actually go
misconceptions.trigger: learner guesses 'email takes a few minutes' without ever timing it
misconceptions.feedback: Log real steps and durations for a few days first. An audit from memory misses the steps that quietly eat the most time.

misconceptions.description: Automating or polishing a step that happens rarely while ignoring the daily repeated one
misconceptions.trigger: learner builds a fancy shortcut for a once-a-term task but retypes the same weekly header by hand
misconceptions.feedback: Target the step that is frequent and slow. Time saved equals frequency times duration, so fix the daily repeat first.

misconceptions.description: Automating a messy process instead of simplifying it first, so the automation just produces mistakes faster
misconceptions.trigger: learner scripts a workflow that still uses wrong file names, spreading the error
misconceptions.feedback: Fix and simplify the process by hand until it is correct, then automate the clean version.

misconceptions.description: Claiming a workflow change helped without measuring time or error rate before and after
misconceptions.trigger: learner says 'this is faster now' with no before time to compare
misconceptions.feedback: Record a baseline (minutes or error count) before the change, then measure again after, so the improvement is evidence not a feeling.
